**Task:** store a large binary (a file, an image) for your app and read it back.

Blobs live outside the app's state: the bytes go to the cluster's blob store,
you get back a content `BlobId`, and you keep that small id in your state. The
store and its replication are in the [blobs reference](/protocol/blobs/).

## Which blobs are your app's

Bytes in the store belong to no one. A blob is your app's once the app's state
**marks** it, and a run can open only blobs its app marks. Two things write a
mark, both as part of an entry in the app's log:

- **An upload.** `POST /apps/{app}/blobs` (or `meroctl blob upload FILE -c
  CONTEXT`) by a caller who may write the app stores the bytes on a majority of
  the cluster's nodes and commits the mark. The answer names the blob.
- **A run that writes one.** `blob_create` → `blob_write`… → `blob_close` in a
  call produces the blob on the run's outcome; the entry's diff marks it.

A node that misses the bytes of a blob its app marks fetches them from another
node of the cluster, so every node can serve every blob of the app.

## The blob API

The SDK exposes a file-descriptor-style API in `calimero_sdk::env`:

| Step | Function | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open a new blob for writing | `blob_create()` | fd (`u64`) |
| Append bytes | `blob_write(fd, &data)` | bytes written |
| Finish writing | `blob_close(fd)` | `BlobId` (`[u8; 32]`) |
| Open one of the app's blobs | `blob_open(&blob_id)` | fd |
| Read bytes | `blob_read(fd, &mut buf)` | bytes read |

Write path: `blob_create` → `blob_write`… → `blob_close` (the returned id is the
content hash). Read path: `blob_open` → `blob_read`… → `blob_close`. Opening a
blob the app does not mark traps.

## Record an uploaded blob

In `apps/blobs` a client uploads the bytes to the app, then calls a method with
the resulting `BlobId`. `env::blob_announce_to_context` answers whether the blob
is the app's — on a cluster there is nothing to announce — so the method can
refuse an id the app does not hold:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::{app, env, AccountId, BlobId};

pub fn upload_file(&mut self, name: String, blob_id: BlobId, size: u64) -> app::Result<String> {
    let current_context = env::context_id();

    if env::blob_announce_to_context(blob_id.as_ref(), &current_context) {
        app::log!("Blob {} is the app's", blob_id);
    } else {
        app::log!("Warning: blob {} is not the app's", blob_id);
    }

    // keep the small id + metadata in state; the bytes stay in the blob store.
    // The id names the uploader and carries a nonce. `files` is an
    // `AuthoredMap`, so the record is the uploader's own entry.
    let mut nonce = [0u8; 8];
    env::random_bytes(&mut nonce);
    let file_id = format!("{}_{}", AccountId::from(env::account_id()), hex(&nonce));
    self.files.insert(file_id.clone(), /* FileRecord { blob_id, name, size, .. } */ )?;
    Ok(file_id)
}
```

<Aside type="caution" title="Name only your own app">
  `blob_announce_to_context` and `blob_open_in_context` take only the **current**
  app (`env::context_id()`); the runtime refuses any other.
</Aside>

## Exercise it

```sh
meroctl blob upload notes.txt -c my-app          # prints the blob id
meroctl call -c my-app upload_file \
  --args '{"name": "notes.txt", "blob_id": "<blob-id>", "size": 12}'
meroctl blob download <blob-id> -c my-app -o notes-copy.txt
```
